subject: economics
title: Minimum Wage and Discrimination
welcome_lead: Two policy hot spots: floors on pay and unequal treatment.
meta_desc: A-Level Labour Markets: minimum wage and discrimination.
final_note: Minimum wages help most workers but risk job loss where demand is elastic.

concepts.def: Wage estimated to cover basic needs.
Unequal pay or hiring not based on productivity.
How responsive employment is to wages.
Reduction in pay gaps after a wage floor.

walkthroughs.body_html: Above the competitive wage, a minimum wage causes unemployment if labour demand is elastic. In a monopsony, it can raise both wages and employment.
Pay gaps may reflect productivity differences (training, hours) or true discrimination. Discrimination is inefficient - it leaves talent unused - and is illegal under equality law.
Anti-discrimination law, pay-gap reporting and equal-pay audits aim to close gaps. Higher minimum wages can compress wages but may push low-skill jobs into automation.

options: Some unemployment if demand is elastic
